Six items today, top pick first.
Flat-memory attention for long documents — keeps memory use flat as the context grows, and the gains hold on small models.
Evaluating agents that call tools — separates task success from its cost and proposes a short checklist for honest comparisons.
Speculative decoding on a phone — twice the generation speed on a mid-range handset with int4 weights.
Probing attention heads for retrieval — a handful of heads do most of the copying; ablating them breaks long-context recall.
A reproducibility note on reward models (discussion).
Yesterday's benchmark was withdrawn by its authors.

content.text: Notes from three low tides on the northern platform, with the open tasks and the arithmetic behind each count.[1]
Count the anemones in pool C[2]
Compare the counts with last season's survey, which used a coarser grid.
Too deep to grid; two counts only
Density is d = n / A for n animals in an area A, so pool C holds:
Pool A was too deep to grid on the second tide, so its estimate rests on two counts. Pool B dried out at the edges, and the count there includes only the wet area. Pool D is new this season.
Each count follows the grid laid at the first tide, read from the seaward corner. The tally sheets are in the appendix, with the photographs filed by pool and tide.
Each visit began an hour before low water.
Anemones closed by the sun were counted once.
Animals on the grid line were counted with the square to their north.
